notes.title: Back from sickness - Dualism is Dragless!
notes.content:
Every once in a while I like to try crazy experiments and change up the gameplay a lot.

This time, I took away air drag for shots. 

I had previously thought the slight exponential change in speed for shots was cool and more natural, but I think this linear, constant speed is better for gaming, and it will likely result in better performance.

So, let me know what you think! I may keep it this way and polish up all the shots speeds for next update. This update, the lack of drag had resulted in changes in speeds for all shots. I have not yet fine tuned these. It's rough. Happy re-exploring! Something different for a while.

It's been like three weeks, what happened to you?!
I'm not sure. I had an ear infection that turned into a really bad fever for a few days, I think. It was the worst I've felt in years. But when it finally went away, it still took me a while to feel 100% normal. In fact, I still feel lethargic and like my brain isn't working like it was before. I went from super productive to super lazy. Gotta 'nother problem to fix now. Myself.

How are the upgrade stats going?
Physical door upgrades was completed. 
New upgrade: Take and give physical hits more often
Returning upgrade: Enemies take physical hits more often

What else?
Water bugs have stopped taking a nap mid-game. This bug also affected the attraction upgrades, so all of these will work much better when there's a lot of enemies on the screen.

Fixed: not dealing the same amount of damage on collision with reflection

Fixed: Bombs drop in every direction on hit 

Slight optimization in calculating enemy health, xp, dmg

Fixed: Ant collision stun length was getting reduced twice when it was injured

~~~

Good luck, and have fun with the new shot speeds this week!

notes.title: Performance down, stability up
notes.content:
Don't upgrade if you want maximum performance at the risk of crashing.

Instance pooling turned off
I think instance pooling, a technique for optimizing framerate when there's a TON of shots on the screen, was slightly instable, and causing weird behavior and crashes sometimes.

I removed this optimization for this build. So there will be about a 10% decrease in performance.

For example, with instance pooling, and 2500 shots on the screen, 65 fps.
Without instance pooling, and same 2500 shots on the screen, 57 fps.

If you still experience any crashes (especially ones without an error report) LET ME KNOW!

Shots upgrade
Also, by request, increased the maximum number of times you can get the "Shots do more damage" upgrade

Week off
I have been struggling with the game updates for the last couple of weeks. I think I need to take a week off, let my creative energy refill, and, probably more importantly, take care of a bunch of things outside of the game that I've been putting off. These things have been nagging me (you need to do this!) constantly for weeks, so I'm going to try and get a bunch of these things done. All to say, there may not be an update at the end of this week. This week, I'm not requiring myself to push an update. I apologize for the delay.

On another note, one of these things will be setting up my office for streaming. So after this I can do things like live coding / streaming.

But anyway, good luck and have fun. See ya in a week or two.

notes.title: Upgrade Stats, part 4: Lightning,. and more Optimization
notes.content:
"Ahhh motherland!"

This week was focused on getting more upgrade stats done, and I got sidetracked with more optimizations. Good thing though, I think there were some interesting ones made that I hadn't thought of before. Getting closer to fully optimized.

Someone want to test me on that?
I believe this version is about 20% more performant than last week's game. 

What's are this week's Upgrade Stats?
Lightning
There were a concerning amount of bugs in the lightning code. For example, it wouldn't even work when there was just two bugs. Now it does, it should chain a lot more, and everything, including those blasted blast sizes, will reduce after each chain. It's optimized as well. Everything is getting a nice coat of optimization now.

What the heck is going on with these particles?
Yeah, they were changed. I was given advice on a different method to do them, and at first, I implemented them with a bug that didn't calculate shot sizes correctly. Then I liked the effect, and decided to keep that bug in the code. It's cleaner. It's also more performant.

Those who don't believe performant is a word will be culled
As much as I wish, again, that more of these upgrade stats were done... one day they will be completed for all 120 or so. The thing is I'm rewriting where all these values are calculated and making sure they're much more consistent. I'm also going over all the math again, and even rebalancing them in many cases. Then it gets crazy with how everything is linked in the game. For example, these are the things that make lightning that all had to be updated and tested: player collisions, all 8 or so shot styles, bombs, chi attack, mosquitos, spikes, spikes made by balls and shields, shields, and balls. Oh and don't forget testing with that last boss! I'm guessing two more weeks to finish these upgrade stats.

Good luck, and have fun.

notes.title: Midweek update: fixes and optimizes
notes.content:
Yoooo

Another week, another mid-week update. (doh!)

Fix
There were some crashes happening due to all the sprites I deleted in the last update. This should be fixed now.

Optimize
I included some optimizations I have been working on. Something called "instance pooling", so certain engine procedures are skipped when creating and destroying thousands of projectiles per second.

And it was a success! I'm seeing anywhere from 5-20% framerate boosts from it.

Reworking
Particles have also changed. I am trying something else to optimize them. A bug in the code caused the particles to look the way they do, and... I kind of like it. So I'm keeping it this way for now. Let me know what you think. Cleaner might be better, when the game is already super-chaotic. 

Be aware
Poison, slow, etc, currently don't show in shot particles. Particles are a work in progress, and I wanted to push this update out quickly to fix the game crashes.

Enjoy~

notes.title: Titan Boss Update
notes.content:
A new boss - The Titan Beetle!
You may "run" into him ;)
He is a very physical boss that relies more on his SHIELD and smashing into you. Chaos, of course, as well. Combined with his diplomatic assets, it's likely he's even more difficult than Harry Legs.

Bosses in general were rewritten a lot. You won't see it, but I made changes that will come in future updates. Future ways to make the game easier or more difficult. The bosses will be able to stack more attacks at a time, for example.

Bosses now announce their moves, "just like my Japanese anime!" This should help players learn not only their attacks, but also how the boss attack system works. 

What else?
Several smaller items:

Mouse captured
No more clicking outside the window. If you need to move the window, you can unlock the mouse by pressing ALT+1. This is also mentioned in Video options.

MothMind stronger
I was getting tired of people telling me MothMind was easy. He's slightly stronger, slightly sturdier, and twice as parasitic.

Bombs un-buffed
Last update had fairly significant upgrades in strength to bombs. It's been set back to previous weeks' values.

Emergency Teleport fixed
Not just fixed. Made better. It had to be modified when it's triggered. Much better balanced now. You can get the upgrade up to three times, at which point you'll teleport to safety whenever you touch something. The area you teleport to is searched for enemies before you teleport. Much better, at least. Most importantly, your balls teleport with you now. Who would use a teleporter if your balls didn't travel with you?!

Importantly, this upgrade was moved from Physical to the Time and Aero doors. It didn't make sense in Physical, since it basically prevents you from developing a very powerful physical build by teleporting you to safety as soon as you get physical.

Spikes balanced
Spikes are a strong tool. But they actually were OP with many spikes and balls. You could create 30+ spikes a second that way. Now, spikes can only be made every 3/4 second, no matter how many spikeable attacks you have.

New engine
Updated to a new GameMaker Studio engine. Supposedly, framerates could increase.

GMLive
If you look in the game files, you'll see GMLive. It's just a tool to help me develop much better. I can see updates in the game without having to recompile, which should make development much faster. I'm excited for it. 

Shots can go out of bounds
Before, I was deleting shots as soon as they left the screen. Now there's a buffer, so tracking shots have some room to come back in.

Player shown on pause and upgrade screens
This was done so you have more information about where your avatar is when you are quickly thrown back into the chaos. Believe it or not, this is also a step toward the main focus next week, which will be:

Next week: stat change information when looking at the different upgrades

Good luck and have fun. Don't let Titan beat you around too much.

notes.title: "No more One Shotted" Update
notes.content:
Tired of building a sweet killer dragonfly only to get obliterated by something you thought you were relatively safe from?

Me too!

Various game balances were put in to try to reduce the chance of this, most importantly:

Max damage per second
Players now have max damage per second capped at 35% of their health. So it should take 3 seconds of total obliteration to finally finish players off now. There's a little breathing room to get out of dodge and get some health now.

Along with a New Upgrade, which reduces max damage per second by 5% each upgrade.

Loading screen with gameplay tips
Just something to round off the game a bit. There's a lot of strategy involved, and hopefully this will continue to teach players after they finish the tutorial.

Doors have more information

 Open a Door screen has tips now, giving a little more information and strategy about the various doors as you hover over them.
 Holding Shift, L1, or R1 on this screen shows you which upgrades are behind the doors. Less mystery, yay!
 Fixed the placement of the already-opened-door icons on this screen too


Various game balances

 Spider boss has his legs set back a little bit, to give the player more room to roam during the fight
 Giant mosquito and kissing bugs had their damage reduced a little, since I kept seeing players getting surprise-obliterated by them. These are some of the "Scary Bugs", if you know what I mean, James and Lee
 Disabled the wider and narrower spread/straight shots until you have multiple of those types of shots. I kept seeing players grab them when they were useless. I need to communicate these upgrades' effects better, but this should be a start.
 Very slightly easier scaling overall. (Probably, especially with the new Max Damage Per Second stat...)


Gameplay change
Screw no longer goes through webs or ants. That was a relic of when screw cost stamina, and stamina is no more. So screw was getting a little over powered in that regard.

There's a little "suggestion" for gun to use- the cursor starts in a random place. Might give 10% more exp for this random selection in the future...

Bug fixes

 Sfx fix when you end the game with screw on
 Wrong sfx was used moving to select gun screen
 'Max focus achieved' messages (achievement unlocked, basically) now appears even when the story is turned off


Linux update

Any new upgrades?
Yes, one:

[upgrade] Balls are attractive

Be careful. Attractive balls invite a lot of potentially unwanted guests trying to touch your balls!

What did you do to help people just starting Dualism?
One of the great struggles with Dualism's development, especially as a roguelike, is making it easy and fun for people brand new to it and deep and challenging for those who invest lots of time. This week's updates are again focused on giving newbies a better time while still keeping it challenging in the later levels.

Yes! SPARKLES! A lot of particle effects, among other things were added, which made the game look radically different. For more information, check out the patch notes. Honestly, I couldn't find the patch notes on Steam, so I won't be doing that anymore. Updates will stick to this format.

notes.title: Massive Rebalancing Update!
notes.content:
It's basically a new game...

So not ALL goals were met this week. I have not put in new code to prevent redundant assets that cause slowdown when the player gets god-tier powerful.

HowEVER! Literally everything in the game changed. I put aside two days this week for making the game more FUN!

Massive Rebalancing
In order to appeal to first timers better, I made the game easier to pick up and play. I realized that I was hitting new players over the head too hard and - yeah - why would they keep coming back? The game needs a learning curve, and I'm starting to put that in. 

You'll notice immediately some of the changes. 

Better initial stats - The Machine Gunner

 Shoot further
 Shoot faster
 Shoot more often (2x)
 Shots do less damage (2x)
 Better turn speed


This could be the start of different initial stats, like- choose your ship before you enter the battlefield.

Yes these are massive changes in the gameplay, and it's my intention to keep doing this throughout development. So please let me know what you think! These updates are coming at the requests of players, so make your voice heard!

What else was rebalanced?

More bugs, but they're all easier to kill
Enemies scale up slower for HP and damage
Reduced most enemy HPs
Your healing scales up slower as well
Boss waves come sooner
Bosses scale separately from regular bugs, and harder
Every enemy that shoots multiple shots at once had their damage halved
Players should be blindsided by death less often now and have more time to GTFO of whatever is killing them rapidly
Poison hits three times as often at three times less power
Common flies easier
Bees, since they are so much harder than flies, are a higher level bug now
Chasing beetles have much less health
Giant mosquitos are easier to kill
Screw half as strong
Spikes hit more removed as it's OP



What else changed that wasn't a rebalance?

[art] New background!
[art] Swaps between backgrounds are smooth as silk and different each run
[art] Doors opened appear on Open Door and Upgrade Screens
[info] Upgrade screen shows how many times you've got each upgrade and which one is the mutation (an upgrade outside of your evolutionary path)
[info] Tips show what level your current upgrade is
[story] Story now plays in order!
[story] Story plays every three minutes, instead of every 7 waves.
[rework] Better collisions code- less likely to get spammed and spam enemies with physical hits
[fix] Collisions went soft and lifeless in the last update. That's fixed. Sorry about that.
[rework] Attraction reworked so it constantly pulls enemies in. Try it! It's fun!
[upgrade] New Upgrade! Screw attracts!
[upgrade] New Upgrade! Spikes attract!
[upgrade] New Upgrade! Mines last longer!
[fix] No more crash when a wrecking ball creates a spike with vampire effect that hits an enemy of the opposite polarity that's supposed to give HP back to the player
[fix] Massive god-tier mine explosions don't kill off-screen enemies waiting to spawn in
[art] Faster blast animations
[art] Screen wrap of pain veins is less intense and distracting
[art] Hit flashes are less intense
[stats and challenges] Game has announcements when you complete challenges
[info] Registered the game with IGDB, so now hopefully it appears in Twitch and Discord
[info] Upgrade screen shows 


So what should we focus on?
Try Attraction!
Upgrade screen has more info!
Get level 9 upgrades!
Try the new rebalance!

What's coming but we can't see yet

 Titan Beetle BOSS - He's been designed. He needs art and implementation now.
 Massively reworked UPGRADE SCREEN. Needs art and implementation now.


Please let me know what you think of the changes!
